requirements.title: Agent protocol and generated code
requirements.rationale: One versioned gRPC protocol whose generated code is checked in keeps `go build` free of generators, and lets the tool schemas come from the tools package byte for byte.

criteria.action: declare package agentkit.sandbox.v1 with a go_package naming sandbox/internal/sandboxpb and a single service Agent with exactly five RPCs: unary Hello, Tools and Call, client-streaming SyncTar(stream TarChunk) returning SyncResponse, and server-streaming ExportTar(ExportRequest) returning stream TarChunk. Tool input, result data and result metadata are carried as JSON bytes fields, never as proto structs
criteria.contract: the package is agentkit.sandbox.v1 and the go_package option ends in sandbox/internal/sandboxpb; there is exactly one service, Agent, with exactly the methods Hello, Tools, Call, SyncTar and ExportTar; Hello, Tools and Call are unary; SyncTar is client-streaming with input TarChunk and output SyncResponse; ExportTar is server-streaming with input ExportRequest and output TarChunk; CallRequest has a string tool-name field and a bytes input field; CallResponse has bool ok, bytes data, string error, string detail, bytes metadata and string text; no field of CallRequest or CallResponse is message-typed (no google.protobuf.Struct, no session or id reference), and the input, data and metadata fields have kind BytesKind

setup: the checked-in sandbox/internal/sandboxpb generated code

fd = sandboxpb.File_sandbox_proto
assert fd.Package() == 'agentkit.sandbox.v1'
assert strings.HasSuffix(fd.Options().GoPackage, 'sandbox/internal/sandboxpb')
assert fd.Services().Len() == 1; svc = fd.Services().Get(0); assert svc.Name() == 'Agent'
assert methodNames(svc) == {Hello,Tools,Call,SyncTar,ExportTar}
assert svc.Method('SyncTar').IsStreamingClient() && !IsStreamingServer()
assert svc.Method('ExportTar').IsStreamingServer() && !IsStreamingClient()
req = fd.Messages().ByName('CallRequest'); resp = ...('CallResponse')
for f in [req.input, resp.data, resp.metadata]: assert f.Kind() == BytesKind
for f in fields(req)+fields(resp): assert f.Kind() != MessageKind

requirements.title: Host API and spec checking
requirements.rationale: Driving every refusal from one function over the provider's Capabilities means that what a provider advertises and what it refuses cannot drift apart.

criteria.action: export AgentPath = "/usr/local/libexec/agentkit-sandboxd"; Spec{Image, Workdir, Env map[string]string, Resources, Network, TTL, Labels, Provider map[string]any}; Resources{CPUs, MemoryBytes, PIDs, DiskBytes}; Network{Mode NetworkMode, Allow []Endpoint} with Endpoint{Host, Port}, and NetworkNone (the zero value), NetworkAllowlist and NetworkUnrestricted; Capabilities{Provider, Isolation, Network, Resources, Image, Workdir, Notes} with IsolationNone, IsolationConfinement, IsolationContainer and IsolationMicroVM; the Provider interface (Capabilities, Create, Reap); the Sandbox interface (ID, Spec, Agent, Sync, Tools, Export, Close); AgentInfo{Version, ProtocolMajor, ProtocolMinor, Workdir, OutlineBackend, Git}; ToolOptions{Symbols tools.SymbolOptions, SpillDir, DisableSpill}; the sealed Source and Destination interfaces, implemented only by Tar{R io.Reader, Path string, Replace bool} and TarOut{W io.Writer}; SyncResult{Files int, Bytes int64}; and the errors ErrUnsupported, ErrProtocol, ErrUnavailable, ErrClosed, ErrToolMismatch, ErrToolsConfigured and ErrUnsafeArchive
criteria.contract: sandbox.AgentPath == "/usr/local/libexec/agentkit-sandboxd"; Spec, Resources, Network, Endpoint, Capabilities, AgentInfo, ToolOptions, Tar, TarOut and SyncResult compile as composite literals with exactly the specified fields and types; NetworkNone is the zero value of NetworkMode, and NetworkAllowlist, NetworkUnrestricted and the four Isolation constants are distinct; Source and Destination each have an unexported method (reflect shows NumMethod counting a non-exported name), Tar implements Source and TarOut implements Destination; ErrUnsupported, ErrProtocol, ErrUnavailable, ErrClosed, ErrToolMismatch, ErrToolsConfigured and ErrUnsafeArchive are non-nil and pairwise not errors.Is-equal

requirements.title: Tar sync and export
requirements.rationale: Tar, using only the standard library, is how this foundation puts a project into a sandbox and gets files out, and the same entry rules apply in both directions.

criteria.action: refuse the operation before any byte moves; `""` and `.` both name the workspace root and are accepted
criteria.contract: Sync or Export returns a non-nil error naming the path, makes no RPC, and leaves the sandbox live

criteria.action: for any tar stream, accept only regular files, directories, and symlinks whose target, resolved against the link's own directory, stays inside the target directory. Refuse an absolute entry name, an entry name with a `..` component, hard links, character and block devices, FIFOs, any other entry type, a symlink whose target leaves the target directory, and an entry whose path resolves through an existing symlink to a location outside. Clear the setuid, setgid and sticky bits of every accepted entry. The same function applies on the agent's extraction and on the host's export validation
criteria.contract: both paths accept the stream if and only if an independent oracle classifies every entry as allowed; when refused, both paths stop at the same first forbidden entry and name it; every accepted file or directory ends with mode & (setuid|setgid|sticky) == 0 on disk and in the validated header; no file is created outside the target directory
